  UPDATE - CITY RESPONSE TO WINDSTORMS AND FIRES -
  CITY MANAGER AND EMERGENCY OPERATIONS STAFF
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Consider updates from City staff and provide direction if desired
  by the City Council; and

Council Minutes  4  01/13/2025
   (2) Find that, if direction is given to staff, it would not be a "project"
  subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant

n  to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and within the
  meaning ofCEQA Guidelines Section 15378(b).

  City Manager Marquez provided a brief recap on the windstorm
  event and the Eaton fire that occurred and began on January 7,
  2025. Chad Augustin, Pasadena Fire Chief, gave a Powerpoint
  presentation on the windstorm and wildfire event timeline, recapped
  the City's preparation efforts, and gave a status update on the City's
  ongoing disaster response and emergency operations. Eugene
  Harris, Pasadena Police Chief, provided an update on the disaster
  response by the Pasadena Police Dept, noting that the incident
  command post has been in operation for the entirety of the disaster.
  Fire Chief Augustin also reported on the rapid expansion of the fire
  and the resources gathered to assist firefighting efforts. City
  Manager Marquez reported that the City is working with numerous
  agencies (FEMA, Red Cross, Kaiser, etc.) to offer resources and
  support to victims, and thanked members of the community for
  coming together to help one another and extended deepest gratitude
  to all the firefighters and first responders for their service and heroic
  efforts.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for the City to look into grants
  to incentivize residents to build ADUs, reduce or waive parking
  permits, and partner with the Pasadena Rental Housing Board to
  assist fire victims with securing temporary housing while they are
  displaced and preparing to rebuild.

  David Reyes, Acting General Manager of Water and Power,
  provided an informational update issues related to water quality in
  the impacted areas of Pasadena. Stacie Takeguchi, Assistant
  General Manager, reported on water quality testing efforts, and
  shared that a large portion of the areas under the Do-Not-Drink
  advisory have been cleared, noting that City staff is working diligently
  to restore service to all other areas. Acting General Manager Reyes
  reported that the City is distributing bottled water during the Do-Not-
  Drink period, and will continue to do so until drinking water quality is
  restored to all residents.

  Councilmember Jones advocated to have a standing committee item
  on the next Municipal Services Committee agenda to discuss the
  recovery and rebuilding efforts for the community. He also suggested
  having an expedited permitting process that would allow victims to
  rebuild faster.

u  Councilmember Cole advocated to have a lengthy City Council
  discussion with public input and staff recommendations on rebuilding
  efforts as recovery efforts proceed. He commended the firefighters
  and first responders for their tremendous efforts.

  Council Minutes  5  01/13/2025
   In response to Vice Mayor Rivas' inquiry regarding masks and
  personal protective equipment (PPE), Manuel Carmona, Acting

n  Public Health Director, reported that the City has ordered PPE and
  will organize distribution for the community once received. In
  response to Vice Mayor Rivas' inquiry regarding price gouging,
  Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor, reported that
  price gouging during the City's Declaration of Emergency is illegal
  and that the City's Prosecutor's Office will pursue prosecutions if
  necessary.

  Councilmember Lyon expressed gratitude and commended City
  staff for their unwavering leadership during the disaster. In response
  to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding the clean-up process,
  Greg de Vinck, Public Works Director, reported that staff is currently
  working on contracts to hire additional assistance to clear the streets
  and impacted areas, and noted that the clean-up process may take
  up to 6 weeks to clear, pulverize, and haul away debris. He reported
  that a site at Hahamonga Park has opened for residents to drop off
  their own green waste debris caused by the windstorm and wildfire.

  Councilmember Madison expressed gratitude for the heroic efforts
  of the first responders and the community's efforts to help one
  another. He advocated for all committees to have discussions on the
  windstorm and wildfire event, within their own appropriate subject
  matter, and report back to the full City Council. He also suggested
  improving communication efforts in the event of another local
  emergency.

  Denise Everhart, representing the American Red Cross, provided an
  update on the sheltering at the Pasadena Convention Center,
  commended City staff on the extraordinary efforts to open this
  shelter and respond so efficiently and effectively to the needs of the
  community, and reported that the Red Cross will be offering hygiene,
  mental health, financial assistance, and other disaster recovery
  resources as well.

  Mayor Gordo praised City staffs preparation for the windstorm and
  the ability to seamlessly transition to the Emergency Operations
  Center (EOC) in response to the windstorm.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that the 14+ letters advocating for a rent
  freeze and/or establishing an eviction moratorium as a result of the
  Eaton Fire, and 3 letters urging the City to waive Rent Control
  provisions to encourage property owners to offer temporary housing
  to tenants displaced by fires, and other related comments, were
  received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council,
  and posted online.

  Council Minutes  6  01/13/2025
   The following individuals advocated for property owners of vacant
  properties to clean up dead trees, branches, and debris to mitigate
  fire risk:

  Emily Duncan, Pasadena resident
  Ashley Sanders, Pasadena resident

  The following individuals advocated for a rent freeze, eviction
  moratorium, and other tenant protections for displaced individuals,
  and/or provided related comments:

  Ryan Bell, Pasadena resident
  Brigitte Rooney, Pasadena resident
  Swantje Willms, Irvine resident
  Ash Riveire, Pasadena resident
  Dar Azimi, Pasadena resident
  Seanna Morgan, Pasadena resident
  Jane Panangaden, Pasadena resident
  Joe Caste), Pasadena resident
  Anthony Manousous, Pasadena resident
  Jo Pimienta, Pasadena resident
  Natalia Govoni, Pasadena resident
  Dan Huynh, Pasadena resident

  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident, requested that the underground
  utility program of the City be reemphasized to protect against
  future fire disasters, and the City's water supply be discussed by
  the City Council.

  The following individuals advocated for temporary revisions/waiver
  of provisions related to Rent Control in the City Charter to allow
  property owners to provide temporary rental housing for those
  displaced by the Eaton fire without being subject to relocation
  assistance at the end of the tenancy:

  Anthony Edson, Pasadena resident
  Simon Gibbons, Pasadena resident

  Christine Lenches-Hinkel, Pasadena resident, advocated for soil
  stabilization and remediation to ensure proper management of
  the pulverization of green waste, and for the City to implement
  preventative measures for possible mudflows.

  Nina Chomsky, Pasadena resident, expressed safety concerns
  and inquired about implementing a curfew for areas under
  evacuation orders within the City.

  Jill Shook, Pasadena resident, inquired about the scope of
  damage within the City caused by the disaster, and expressed
  concerns regarding the future sale of impacted properties that

Council Minutes  7  01/13/2025
   belong to African American families and vulnerable members of
  the community.

n  Yadi, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns regarding the
  cause of the Eaton Fire, the safety of the water and air, and the
  City's communication efforts to provide updates to the public.

  Tim Martinez, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City to
  conduct air quality testing and expressed concerns regarding
  contaminated water in the City's water supply.
